title: Watchmen: The End is Nigh
provenance: Reported by udance4ever (highball-db#941, 2026-11-03), Apple M1, macOS 27.2, Highball 0.10.24, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r29, D3DMetal, rated 1 of 5 after 4 minutes: DirectX installs, then MultiLauncher.exe says the .NET Framework must be enabled in Windows Features, with the dotnet48 recipe installed. Not verified by the maintainer. udance4ever offered on highball-db#941 (2026-11-03) to install .NET 3.5 with winetricks' dotnet35 verb, tried on 2026-11-25 (below). udance4ever again (highball-db#941, 2026-11-25): highball tricks with dotnet35 stopped at winetricks' 'Cannot find cabextract' on the Wine 10 engine r31, also with Homebrew's cabextract installed. The CLI gives winetricks a PATH of the engine's and the system's folders only, and finds the app's cabextract only when the code runs inside the app or HIGHBALL_TOOLS points to it, which a CLI built from the repository doesn't do on its own. udance4ever again later that day (highball-db#941, 2026-11-25): with HIGHBALL_TOOLS pointing to the app's tools folder, cabextract was found and dotnet35 ran for a few minutes. Then ServiceModelReg.exe, part of .NET 3.0's Windows Communication Foundation, crashed into Wine's debugger on the Wine 10 engine r31, and highball tricks hadn't returned when the comment was written. A CLI built with highball#795 looks for the app only in /Applications and ~/Applications, and this player's Highball.app is in a folder inside /Applications.
notes: Doesn't start in one report on an M1. Its MultiLauncher.exe asks for the .NET Framework to be enabled, though .NET 4.8 is installed in the environment. It's a 32-bit game.

knownIssues.symptom: MultiLauncher.exe says the .NET Framework must be enabled from Windows Features, with .NET 4.8 installed
knownIssues.cause: not diagnosed. PCGamingWiki says the game needs .NET Framework 3.5, which .NET 4.8 doesn't provide, so the launcher most likely wants 3.5 (inferred, not checked here)
knownIssues.fix: none in Highball yet. Winetricks has a dotnet35 verb, not yet run to the end with this game. Through the CLI's 'highball tricks', with HIGHBALL_TOOLS set to the app's Contents/Resources/tools folder, cabextract is found and the .NET 3.5 installer runs, then ServiceModelReg.exe crashed into Wine's debugger and the command didn't return (Wine 10 r31, highball-db#941, 2026-11-25). Whether closing Wine's crash window lets the installer finish isn't known yet
